title: Research workspace reset and experiment-memory migration
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A minimal active workspace plus normalized experiment memory will reduce route confusion without losing expensive reusable assets.
material_change: Replace thousands of legacy reports/scripts/checkpoints with one fixed experiment index, one baseline, one compact teacher, and cold storage for expensive evidence.
baseline: 4294 reports, 2687 AlphaHoldem files, 294.9 GiB models, and 227.0 GiB data
notes: Post-cleanup train_v5 smoke completed 100 environment hands, performed one PPO update, wrote a finished checkpoint, and changed weights; smoke artifacts were then removed.

result.summary: Normalized 37 historical records, retained one exact Standard10 baseline and one compact 200bb teacher, cold-stored 163.2 GiB, and permanently removed about 357.8 GiB of redundant research data.
result.conclusion: The active research surface is small, reproducible, and no longer exposes legacy route clutter by default.
result.next_step: Begin future learned-policy experiments through the fixed experiment log.
